content.title: fillip - Wiktionary, the free dictionary
content.text: From Wiktionary, the free dictionary From Middle English filippen, philippe (“to flick or snap a finger from against the thumb”);[1] further origin uncertain, but probably imitative.[2] See flip. It is not clear whether the verb is derived from the noun, or vice versa.[2][3] (Received Pronunciation, General American) IPA(key): /ˈfɪlɪp/ Homophones: Philip, Phillip Hyphenation: fil‧lip fillip (plural fillips) (archaic) The action of holding the tip of a finger against the thumb and then releasing it with a snap; a flick. quotations ▼ A sharp strike or tap made using this action, or (by extension) by other means. quotations ▼ (by extension) Something unimportant, a trifle; also, the brief time it takes to flick one's finger (see noun sense 1); a jiffy. quotations ▼ (by extension) Something that excites or stimulates. quotations ▼This measure gave a fillip to the housing market. The athlete’s victory provided a much-needed fillip for national pride. show ▼±action of holding the tip of a finger against the thumb and then releasing it with a snap show ▼±smart strike or tap made using the fingers something unimportant — see trifle brief period of time — see jiffy show ▼±something that excites or stimulates fillip (third-person singular simple present fillips, present participle filliping or (archaic) fillipping, simple past and past participle filliped or (archaic) fillipped) (transitive) To strike, project, or propel with a fillip (that is, a finger released quickly after being pressed against the thumb); to flick. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: flick, ping (transitive, by extension) To project quickly; to snap. quotations ▼ (transitive, by extension) To strike or tap smartly. quotations ▼ (transitive, figuratively) To drive as if by a fillip (noun sense 1); to excite, stimulate, whet. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: inflame; see also Thesaurus:thrill The spicy aroma filliped my appetite. (ambitransitive) To make a fillip (noun sense 1) (with the fingers). quotations ▼ filliping (noun) flip (possibly) show ▼±to make a fillip (with the fingers) ^ “filippen, v.”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 23 July 2019. ↑ Jump up to: 2.0 2.1 “fillip, n.”, in OED Online ⁠, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1896; “fillip, n.”, in Lexico, Dictionary.com; Oxford University Press, 2019–2022. ^ “fillip, v.”, in OED Online ⁠, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1896; “fillip, v.”, in Lexico, Dictionary.com; Oxford University Press, 2019–2022.
